per_run.note: deliberate design choice: found StatusEmailConfirmationRequired and chose to attach when the provider asserts the address verified (audit confidence medium)

b1.summary: Every run fixed the reported verified-email gate, refused with a 4xx and carried the assertion through the token/profile merge (T1 and T2 passed in all 6). Two failures decide the result. (a) T4: 5 of 6 runs attach a provider-verified sign-in to a local account still in StatusEmailConfirmationRequired (the callback rejects only disabled/locked accounts). (b) T3: 2 runs declared email_verified as a plain Go bool, so a string "true" breaks decoding and a sign-in that works today fails (the only cause of DS run 3).

b2.note: One security test decides 5 of 6 runs and is the only security failure in any run. Without it, 4 runs score 1.0 and DS reaches 2 of 3 solved.

b3.note: Every run except mimo 01:21 is exactly one failing test from 1.0.

b4.note: The same T4 omission in 5/6 runs (one of them a deliberate choice), plus the same strict-bool decoder regression in 2 runs.

b5.open_human_question: FAIRNESS.md (2026-10-24 22:23, after the v2 instruction of 15:07, before the 10-25 trials) asks a human to confirm three things. (1) THE T4 READING: does the confirmation-required state count among 'protections the product already applies', so that a provider's verified assertion must not license confirming and linking? This is the decisive test in 5/6 runs, and both medium-confidence audits are T4-decided (DS 01:03 chose that alternative reading on purpose). (2) Which single test produced DS's 5/6: now answered by qa_runs (TestSec_UnconfirmedLocalAccountIsNotLinked). (3) Whether a refusal contract stricter than published fix B is intended. No resolution of (1) or (3) is recorded.

b6.reason: Checked against the real upstream commit 7854f2729ab7 (GHSA-xv7q-fvmc-jx96). It adds the boolish decoder for string email_verified (covers T3) and copies EmailVerified with the address in mergeClaims (covers T2, so the manifest's 'uncovered_upstream' label on T2 is wrong). It never checks StatusEmailConfirmationRequired: the word 'confirm' appears 0 times in the patch, so T4, which decides 5/6 runs, survives a fix lookup. DS run 3 was decided only by T3, which upstream covers. Also, upstream falls through to creating a separate account, so copying it fails all 6 security tests under the instruction's refusal contract (gate: upstream_fix = 6 security fails).

quotes: An external sign-in must not attach to an existing local account in a way that bypasses protections the product already applies to that account.
An address the provider does not assert as verified is not verified.
Fix the problem and its close variants
b7.note: listing.json: T1 NAMED (reported route), T4 DESCRIBED (the protections clause, without naming the confirmation state), T2 and T3 GENERAL. The decisive T4 is pointed at abstractly, and 5 of 6 runs still missed it.

c1.mechanism: authentication bypass / account takeover through OIDC email-fallback account linking (unverified address, unconfirmed local account)
c1.domain: to-do / project-management web app (Vikunja), OpenID Connect sign-in

c2.note: The manifest labels T4 'injection_room', but it is real unmodified code (the callback checks only disabled/locked) and the real fix does not cover it, so in substance it is uncovered-upstream. Secondary keep-working-value 'over-strict decoding of legitimate input' (T3, covered upstream). The build score flagged single-trap-carries (score 0.275, without the hardest 0.011).

e2.why: All 6 runs trusted, model-failed; 4 high and 2 medium. Both medium runs are T4-decided.

e3.why: READY, but NEEDS_HUMAN_REVIEW: YES is open on the exact reading of the T4 sentence that decides 5/6 runs. One run chose the contested reading on purpose.

e4.why: TestSec_UnconfirmedLocalAccountIsNotLinked (a session issued for an unconfirmed local account) decides 5/6 runs.

e5.why: Upstream 7854f272 has no confirmation-state check; T4 is uncovered.

concerns: The decisive T4 depends on a vague sentence ('protections the product already applies'). Reading a provider-verified address as satisfying local confirmation is defensible. DS 01:03 reasoned its way there, and the fairness review left exactly this for a human, unresolved.

T4's real-world harm is unverified (notes.md: 'T4's real-world harm ... could not verify'; the attacker cannot log into an unconfirmed account with a mailer configured). A weak-impact trap carrying the breaker invites a fairness or realism challenge.
Fragile: one security test decides 5/6 runs, and every run but one is one test short of 1.0.
DS run 3 is decided only by a keep-working value (string email_verified) that the public fix covers.
Manifest origin labels are wrong against the real commit (T2 'uncovered_upstream' is covered; T4 'injection_room' is real, uncovered code). Fix them before pattern tallies.
The blind fix was never produced (extract error).

Test quality gaps from the fairness review: victim-row mutation before refusal is not checked; the refusal helper is tight (no echo.HTTPError); TestSec_VerificationOfAnotherAddress may never reach mergeClaims.
one_line: Vikunja OIDC email-linking takeover where both models add the reported verified-email gate but still link a provider sign-in to a local account that has not confirmed its own address, a check the public fix also lacks.
